name: ICLR
notes: Main conference paper track. A genuine abstract and the complete author list are required by the earlier abstract deadline; all authors need OpenReview profiles. The call specifies AoE dates without a clock time. The Dates page lists April 26-30, but the venue is unannounced. The closed 2027 submission schedule supplies the next-cycle estimate basis.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Learning objectives, generative methods, and explanations of neural representations. Connect a specific model behavior to an underlying mechanism, then use that understanding to improve training, inference, or control of generated outputs.
guide.evidence: Comparisons across tasks and model sizes, targeted ablations, and measurements of internal representations. Generative work evaluates output quality and controllability; analysis work tests theoretical predictions through interventions and controlled changes to the model.

comparisons.difference: ICLR and ICML study learning methods and model behavior. ICLR work uses interventions to explain representations and control generation; ICML work tests learning objectives, generalization bounds and data or compute scaling.

ICLR work explains internal model behavior and tests changes to learning or generation. NeurIPS work also measures attribution fidelity, fairness, memory use and speed, alongside prediction or generation quality.

name: NeurIPS
fullName: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
notes: Main paper track only; other tracks have separate calls. Abstracts precede papers, and all authors need an OpenReview profile. Supplementary material is due with the paper. The sources specify AoE dates without a clock time. The event shown is Sydney; Atlanta and Paris programs run December 9-13. The 2026 schedule supplies the next-cycle estimate basis.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: New learning systems, formal analyses, and diagnostic frameworks for understanding existing models. Contributions can explain an observed behavior, make predictions or representations more reliable, or combine components into a more capable and efficient system.
guide.evidence: Tests across datasets or modalities, comparisons with established methods, and experiments that isolate the proposed explanation or component. Evaluations combine task performance with the relevant secondary measures, such as attribution fidelity, group fairness, memory use, or inference speed.

comparisons.difference: NeurIPS and ICLR use ablations and controlled experiments to explain model behavior. NeurIPS work tests attribution, fairness and multimodal systems; ICLR work examines representations, generation control and inference-time learning.

NeurIPS work measures model reliability, attribution, fairness and system efficiency. AAAI work also tests explicit planning and reasoning procedures, counting solved problems and measuring search cost or answer accuracy.

name: AAAI
notes: Main technical track only, with mandatory abstract submission and two-phase review. The official call updates the author feedback window to October 24-31. Its camera-ready entry is struck through, so no camera-ready deadline is assumed. The closed 2027 submission schedule supplies the next-cycle estimate basis.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Algorithms and systems that improve planning, reasoning, or learning under concrete constraints. Combine symbolic search, learned components, retrieval, or annotation strategies to solve tasks more reliably or with less computation and supervision.
guide.evidence: Comparisons across problem domains or benchmark datasets, with ablations of the proposed mechanisms. Measures follow the task: solved planning instances and resource limits, reasoning accuracy or answer overlap, and predictive performance under different annotation budgets and model configurations.

comparisons.difference: AAAI work combines planning, reasoning and learning, evaluated through solved tasks, answer accuracy and annotation cost. ICML work focuses on learning objectives and generalization, tested through formal analysis and controlled data or compute changes.
AAAI work tests search, retrieval and annotation strategies on concrete tasks. NeurIPS work also analyzes models through attribution fidelity, fairness and efficiency across datasets or modalities.

name: ICML
notes: Main paper track; abstracts are mandatory and supplementary material is due with the paper. The CFP labels January 23/28 AoE and explicitly equates them to January 24/29 at 12:00 UTC; the exact UTC cutoffs are preserved here. The 2026 schedule supplies the next-cycle estimate basis. Only the South America region is announced for 2027; its submission schedule and event dates were unavailable when checked.

publication.note: Papers publish in Proceedings of Machine Learning Research (PMLR), a proceedings series, not a journal track.

guide.contribution: Learning objectives, generalization analyses, and controlled investigations of model capabilities. A contribution often identifies a specific limitation, explains it mathematically or experimentally, and develops an algorithm or diagnostic that applies across learning problems.
guide.evidence: Formal derivations or bounds where relevant, comparisons across models and tasks, and controlled changes to training data or computation. Common evaluation questions concern generalization to held-out cases, scaling behavior, efficiency, and whether observations support the proposed explanation.

comparisons.difference: ICML and ICLR study learning algorithms and representations. ICML work tests formal objectives, generalization and scaling; ICLR work uses model interventions and ablations to explain behavior and improve generation or inference.

ICML work evaluates how learning objectives and training conditions affect generalization and efficiency. AAAI also develops explicit search and planning systems, measured through solved instances, resource limits and reasoning accuracy.
